Has received no more than 28 days of treatment.
Has no evidence of grade 2 or greater treatment adverse events (side effects) possibly related to treatment with the EGFR TKI.

A positron emission tomography (PET)-computed tomography (CT) scan within the last 60 days shows radiographic stage I to IIIa lung cancer (a biopsy of the lymph nodes in the middle of the chest is allowed but not required).

A brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan (or a CT scan if an MRI is not possible) within the last 60 days shows no evidence of metastatic disease (cancer that has spread from another part of the body).

Has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status (PS) score of 0 to 1.

Has any unresolved toxicities (side effects) from prior therapy that are greater than Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grade 1 at the time of starting study treatment, with the exception of alopecia (hair loss) and grade 2 prior platinum therapy-related neuropathy (nerve damage) which is allowed.
Has an aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) level of no more than 2.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN).

Bilirubin is no more than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN). Patients with documented Gilbert's syndrome and conjugated bilirubin within the normal range may be allowed into the study; in this event, it will be documented that the patient was eligible based on conjugated bilirubin levels.
Potassium and magnesium levels are within the normal range; patients may receive supplements to meet this requirement.
Has a leukocyte (white blood cell) count of more than 3,000/microliter (mcL).
Has a hemoglobin (a protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen) level of at least 9 g/dL, with no blood transfusions in the 28 days before study entry.
Has an absolute neutrophil count (a type of white blood cell) of more than 1,500/mcL.
Has a platelet count (a type of blood cell that helps with clotting) of more than 100,000/mcL.

Creatinine Clearance (CrCl) (a measure of kidney function) is more than 50 mL/min for patients with serum creatinine (SCr) (a waste product in the blood) that is more than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN).
Has the ability to swallow oral medications.
Has a negative serum pregnancy test (a blood test for pregnancy) within 3 days before the first dose of study treatment.
Agrees to use highly effective contraception (birth control that prevents pregnancy) during the study and for 90 days after the last dose of osimertinib.
Women between their first menstrual period (menarche) and menopause who have not had permanent or surgical sterilization and can become pregnant.

attempts.plain: Women of childbearing potential (WoCBP): women between their first menstrual period (menarche) and menopause who have not had permanent or surgical sterilization and can become pregnant.
Women who are not of childbearing potential: women who are permanently or surgically sterilized or postmenopausal.

Permanent sterilization includes hysterectomy (removal of the uterus) and/or bilateral oophorectomy (removal of both ovaries) and/or bilateral salpingectomy (removal of both fallopian tubes), but excludes bilateral tubal occlusion (blocking or tying the fallopian tubes without removing them). Tubal occlusion is considered a highly effective method of birth control but does not absolutely exclude the possibility of pregnancy.

Women who have had tubal occlusion (a procedure to block the fallopian tubes) are managed on trials as if they are of WoCBP (women of childbearing potential), for example by undergoing pregnancy testing as required by the study protocol.
